newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: The rand see-sawed to a slightly weaker close on Thursday after initially sagging three cents to a fresh seven-month against a rampant U.S. dollar.
Initially, the rand came under pressure from what one dealer terms aggressive dollar demand from players who had gone short overnight for the weekend carry.
The morning move was coupled with the dollar's fresh assault on the 1.89 level in early European trade.

That drove the rand to its day's weakest level of 4.7055 bid -- its lowest level since January 6 -- where dealers said the Reserve Bank supplied liquidity by offering dollars at the 4.70 and 4.7050 levels.

The rand then idled around the upper end of a 4.6950 to 4.70 range before the dollar retreated to below 1.88 marks amid concerns that Germany might hike interest rates next week to defend its currency which has taken a pasting from the dollar in recent months.
"At that point the market was long dollars and with the dollar/mark falling, they started cutting," a trader said.
Another dealer said the dollar's retracement coincided with a hefty dollar order from offshore.
"We saw a big order from offshore and there was very little holding it back and we came right back down," he said.
At 1400 GMT, the rand had firmed back to the 4.6820/6850 level -- just over a cent weaker from its 4.6715/6745 level at 1400 GMT on Wednesday.
By contrast, the rand put in a strong performance against sterling after cable was pummelled lower by perceptions that Britain had reached the peak of its interest rate cycle for now.
The Bank of England earlier raised U.K. interest rates by 25 basis points to 7.00 percent, saying this brought U.K. interest rates to levels consistent with its medium-term inflation target.
Cable's resultant retreat helped the rand/sterling cross firm to its strongest level since June 19 when it traded at 7.4070. It was last trading at 7.4209/4303 from 7.4668/4763 overnight.
Against the mark, the rand was little changed at 0.4003/4008 from 0.4017/4021, while against the yen it was at 25.2294/2669 from 25.4695/4966.
Bonds took fright at the rand's initial weakness against the dollar and ran up to the 14.10 percent level by 0700 GMT from an overnight close of 14.00 percent ahead of the noon close-out.

"We started around the late trade levels of yesterday then all of a sudden the 4.70 level in the rand was a bit of a scarce and at the same time we saw some paper coming out which kicked it up rather violently," a dealer said.
"The options close-out played a role although I would think the impact on the yields was not that massive," he added.

Dealers said that the bulk of the afternoon had been spent cleaning out positions and reassessing the market. With little in the way of direction likely to be on offer on Friday, dealers said yields were likely to idle around current levels before taking a stab at heading lower again next week.
The R150 was last quoted at 14.125 percent from 14.10 percent on Wednesday.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners bought a net 181.41 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling a net 89.06 million rand's worth on Tuesday.
Turnover was 15.1 billion rand compared with Monday's 9.65 billion rand.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 8.446 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.985 billion rand on Tuesday.
Offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.40 to 15.50 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 14.90 percent.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
